subject: URGENT: Quadrant Health experiencing persistent 5xx and latency in us-east-2 — routing fallback requested
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <ezhao@quadranthealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@quadranthealth.com
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: High latency + 5xx from our East region — urgent

Laura,

We started seeing sustained 500 errors and 300-800ms tail latency on our API calls hitting us-east-2 at ~08:50 ET. It looks like a spike in token timeouts and a stream of rejected requests. This is hitting our production users and a scheduled batch job is failing repeatedly.

Attached is a short sample of recent request IDs and latency samples (quadrant_latency_log_0323.csv). We need immediate remediation and to understand whether you can route our traffic away from the impacted AZ while this is investigated.

Can you confirm Redwood can failover Quadrant to an alternate region or a compatible model variant without token loss? We need an ETA and whether this will cause any behavioral differences for our inference (we use reranking + chat).

—Emily
Head of Platform, Quadrant Health

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Emily Zhao <ezhao@quadranthealth.com>, ops@quadranthealth.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 09:23:10 -04:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx from our East region — urgent

Emily — thanks for flagging and for the logs.

Quick status: we see error amplification in us-east-2 AZ3 starting 08:46 ET and an elevated 5xx rate concentrated on requests routed to a specific inference pool. Our on-call team is already isolating the pool and running deeper kernel-level metrics.

Immediate steps I am initiating now (ETA inlined):
- Request-level mitigation: divert new traffic for Quadrant's routes to us-east-1 and us-west-2 while we triage (ETA: 6–12 minutes).
- Preserve KV cache and tokens: we will prefer compatible model variant pinned in your config to avoid latent quality regressions.
- Post-failover verification: run smoke evaluation set and replay a subset of requests to verify parity (ETA: 30m).

Dylan (cc) — please take lead on the diversion and confirm whether we need an emergency hotfix. Marissa, loop in exec if we anticipate credits or a priority call.

Emily — I will send an internal update with timelines and a link to the playbook and Jira.

—Laura
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Emily Zhao <ezhao@quadranthealth.com>, ops@quadranthealth.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 09:31:55 -04:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx from our East region — urgent

Taking point. Short running log: I see KV cache saturation on the pool handling Quadrant's traffic and a sudden increase in long-sequence requests; this is pushing kernel selection into a slow path and causing queue amplification.

Action plan being executed now:
1) Activate route override for Quadrant -> temporary pin to model-redwood-7b-compat in us-east-1 (traffic mirrored to us-east-2 for diagnostics) — expected minutes.
2) Force smaller batch sizes for Quadrant to avoid queue build-up on the fallback pool (applied).
3) Start a limited replay (last 30 minutes) against pinned variant to validate scoring differences (Rishi to own).

I will update the Jira (SRV-4231) with per-step timestamps. If the pinned model shows >3% regression in our smoke metrics, we'll run a canary on a fraction of traffic vs. full swap.

—Dylan
Support Engineering Manager

Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx from our East region — urgent

Looping in exec-level context. Laura / Dylan — please confirm these points for Quadrant's leadership call in 20 minutes:
- Confirmed duration of impact and customer-facing ETA for full restoration.
- Whether automatic fallback to alternate region will be seamless or require a short maintenance window.
- Any appetite for a one-time service credit — Quadrant is SLA-sensitive and their legal/procurement team is on standby.

Emily — my ask to you for the call: are there particular SLAs or contract clauses we should be mindful of (example: per-request SLO or spike credits)? We'll prepare a short readout for your execs.

Operational note for the team: include the attached proposed-geo-swap-plan_v1.pdf that documents the routing steps and cache-preservation safeguards. If we escalate to an org-wide priority, I will request the incident bridge and CEO notice.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Success

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Emily Zhao <ezhao@quadranthealth.com>
Cc: aws-incident@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 13:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx from our East region — urgent

Update summary and closeout steps:

Status at 13:47 ET — diversion complete and stable. Traffic for Quadrant is fully routed to us-east-1 and us-west-2 per the proposed plan; mirrored sampling to us-east-2 continues for diagnostics. 5xxs have dropped to baseline and tail latency is within SLA.

What we did technically:
- Route override applied via smart-router policy (priority: customer-pin > latency-based) — no token reissuance required.
- Batch-size throttling reduced from 64 -> 24 for Quadrant to avoid queue buildup on fallback.
- Applied kernel compatibility switch to force quantized fast path for mirrored workload.

Customer impact notes:
- Short-lived increase (~2–3%) in token consumption for a 15 minute window during the swap due to duplication/mirroring.
- No observed semantic regressions in chat/rerank checks (smoke set passed).

Next steps / Postmortem actions:
1) Full incident postmortem (owner: operations) with timeline and kernel trace attached (Jira SRV-4231).
2) Follow-up remediation: pin additional capacity in us-east-1 for Quadrant for 72h; consider quantization profile update if we see recurrence.
3) Customer comms: Laura / Marissa to confirm exec note and any credit.

Emily — apologies for the disruption. We will attach the diagnostic traces and a short reconciliation of the tokens/requests to the Jira link above by EOB. Happy to jump on a short exec bridge if helpful.

—Rishi
Head of Service Reliability
